All 54 tests across all simple parser test classes pass. Here's a summary of the two fixes:

**Bug 1** — `SimplePredicateParser.java` line 560: The error thrown when the right-hand side of a logical operator is invalid had two problems:
1. The error message said `left.getToken()` — changed to `right.getToken()` so the message names the actual offending token
2. The exception index was `token.getToken().getIndex()` (the `&&` operator itself) — changed to `right.getToken().getIndex()` so the index points at the invalid right-hand token (e.g., index 20 for `"${body} == 'foo' && && ..."`)

**Bug 2** — `LogicalExpression.java`: Both `acceptLeftNode` and `acceptRightNode` unconditionally accepted every node and returned `true`. They now only accept `BinaryExpression` or `LogicalExpression` nodes (the only node types that are valid predicate operands for `&&`/`||`), returning `false` for anything else. Without this fix, the error path in Bug 1 was unreachable because invalid operands were silently accepted.

All 54 tests across all simple parser test classes pass. Here's a summary of the two fixes:

**Bug 1** — `SimplePredicateParser.java` line 560: The error thrown when the right-hand side of a logical operator is invalid had two problems:
1. The error message said `left.getToken()` — changed to `right.getToken()` so the message names the actual offending token
2. The exception index was `token.getToken().getIndex()` (the `&&` operator itself) — changed to `right.getToken().getIndex()` so the index points at the invalid right-hand token (e.g., index 20 for `"${body} == 'foo' && && ..."`)

**Bug 2** — `LogicalExpression.java`: Both `acceptLeftNode` and `acceptRightNode` unconditionally accepted every node and returned `true`. They now only accept `BinaryExpression` or `LogicalExpression` nodes (the only node types that are valid predicate operands for `&&`/`||`), returning `false` for anything else. Without this fix, the error path in Bug 1 was unreachable because invalid operands were silently accepted.
